  4. My parents are controlling narcissistic assholes, so i would never personally consider moving back; but if your situation is better than mine, it might get you a few months of financial stability while you decide what to do next. Just dont get stuck there.

As a parent who had a child in a similar situation, I drove three states away just before christmas (two christmas's ago) and brought her back to the nest so she could get her life back in order. She's just finished her LPN program and starting on her RN. So I'd say it helped.

However! Don't take your parents willingness to bring you back home for granted. I'd give the shirt off my back for my kids if they needed it, but not without discussion. If they need money you better bet I'm asking why and what needs to be done to get them in a position where they don't need to ask for help.

My suggestion is this; if you have other options don't move back in with your parents. Use them as a last resort/keep yourself from living in a cardboard box type of thing. As another poster mentioned, you'll be much happier with yourself if you can get through life's little bumps on your own. If you do decide to move in with your parents, get a full time job, make a plan to move out and discuss it with your parents. You are their child, but at this age your also a disruption to the life they've made for themselves since you moved out. They might just want it back sooner or later. If you can show them you have a plan to get back on your own feet they'll feel better about you staying there.
